summary: Carlo Formichi (1871–1943) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied under Michele Kerbaker, Paul Deussen at Kiel University, Hermann Oldenberg, and Georg Bühler. He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (1898) and Sapienza University of Rome (1914–1941).

Carlo Giussani (1840–1900) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863), as well as under Albrecht Weber (1863), Giuseppe Bardelli (~1863–1865), and Rudolf von Roth (~1865–1866).
Carlo Jamelle Harris is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA in philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin.

Carmen Blacker (1924–2009) specialized in Japanology and religious studies. She studied at SOAS, Somerville College, Oxford, Keio University, and under Shigeru Gorai. She served as assistant lecturer (1955) and Lecturer in Japanese (1958) at Cambridge, and Folklore Society president (1982–1984).

Carmen Dragonetti (1937–2018) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy after studying at the National University of San Marcos (~1957–1961). She held posts at the Fundación Instituto de Estudios Budistas (~1989–2018), IIBS (1989), and Nyingma Institute (1996).

Carmen Meinert (born 1969) is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who earned her PhD from the University of Bonn in 2001. She has held posts at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008), Ruhr University Bochum, and Käte Hamburger Kolleg.

Carol A. Breckenridge (1942–2009) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1976) and held a post at the University of Chicago (~1988–1999).

Carol S. Anderson is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman. She has served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College.

Carola Roloff (born 1959), a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and with Geshe Thubten Ngawang. She held posts at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg, CIHTS, and the University of Hamburg (2018–2025).
Carola S. Carstens is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Hamburg (-2005). She held a post at Rice University (1998–1999).
Carole M. Cusack (born 1962) specializes in religious studies. She studied at the University of Sydney from 1988 to 1995 and held a post there in 2013.

Carole McGranahan (born 1969) specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at Colgate University and the University of Michigan under Nicholas Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler, among others. She joined the University of Colorado as Assistant Professor of Anthropology (~2001–2008).

Caroline Humphrey (born 1943) works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and Indology. She studied at Cambridge (under Edmund Leach) and Leeds. She held posts at the University of Cambridge (1971–2010), Girton College, King's College, and Michigan (2000).

Caroline Rhys Davids (1857–1942) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. She studied at University College London and under T. W. Rhys Davids and Reinhold Rost. She served at the Pali Text Society (1907–1942), Manchester (1910–1913), and SOAS (1918–1933).

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who received her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington (attested 1990). She held posts at Ohio State University and Denison University (attested 1990).
Carson Schütze (born 1968) is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1997.

Catherine Bell (1954–2008) was a religious studies and sinology scholar. She studied under Joseph M. Kitagawa at the University of Chicago Divinity School (~1977–1983) and was Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

Catherine Elaine Prueitt specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She completed a BA at the University of Rochester (-2007) and a PhD at Emory University (-2016), studying under Laurie L. Patton and supervisor John D. Dunne.

Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher (1946–2023) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Minnesota (~1975–1984) and served there as an assistant professor (~1980–2021).

Catherine Ludvik specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. She completed her PhD at the University of Toronto under David Waterhouse, Antonino Forte, Yuko Matsuda, and Werner Knobl. She has held posts at Hanazono University and ISEAS.
